title: Grade 8 Integrated Science Scheme of Work: Energy Transfer (Synthetic Mock Corpus)
subject: Integrated Science

entries.topic: Energy transfer: Energy stores and transfers
learningOutcomes: Identify chemical, kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential and thermal energy stores
Describe energy transfers by mechanical work, electrical current, heating and waves (light and sound)
State that energy is conserved and is measured in joules
keyConcepts: energy cannot be created or destroyed
learningActivities: Learners roll a ball down a ramp and describe the changes in energy stores
Learners investigate a stretched elastic band, a swinging pendulum and a hand warmer
Learners draw energy transfer diagrams for a torch, a bouncing ball and a person eating a meal then running
Learners match everyday devices to the energy transfers they cause
entries.assessment: Describe the energy transfers when a battery-powered torch is switched on.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners often say energy is 'used up' or 'made'; stress that energy is transferred and the total remains the same. Avoid naming energy as a substance that flows like a liquid. Always state the store the energy starts in and where it ends up.

entries.topic: Energy transfer: Conduction, convection and radiation
priorKnowledge: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases
learningOutcomes: Describe conduction as the transfer of energy through vibrating particles in solids
Explain convection in liquids and gases using changes in density
Describe radiation as the transfer of energy by infrared waves that does not need particles
keyConcepts: hot fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises
learningActivities: Learners heat one end of metal rods with wax and pins attached and time how quickly pins fall
Learners observe convection currents by placing a potassium permanganate crystal at the bottom of a beaker of water and gently warming one side (teacher demonstration)
Learners compare the temperature rise of a black can and a shiny can placed near a lamp
Learners classify everyday situations as conduction, convection or radiation
resources: Metal rods of different materials, wax, pins, burner or hot-water bath
Black and shiny cans, lamp, thermometers
entries.assessment: Explain how energy from the Sun reaches Earth and why conduction and convection cannot transfer it.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners often say 'heat rises' or 'cold travels'; it is warm air that rises because it is less dense. Many learners think radiation needs air; infrared radiation travels through a vacuum. Supervise heating and hot water.

entries.topic: Energy transfer: Efficiency and wasted energy
learningOutcomes: Calculate efficiency using useful energy output divided by total energy input x 100%
Explain what happens to wasted energy and why it is not destroyed
Suggest ways to reduce energy waste such as insulation and lubrication
keyConcepts: wasted energy dissipates to the surroundings as thermal energy
learningActivities: Learners compare LED and filament lamps using data on input and useful output energy and calculate efficiency
Learners draw Sankey diagrams for a motor and a lamp
Learners test cups with and without lids or insulation and measure cooling
Learners suggest design changes to reduce energy waste in a device
resources: Graph paper and Sankey diagram templates
entries.assessment: A motor takes in 200 J of electrical energy and transfers 150 J usefully. Calculate its efficiency and state where the remaining energy goes.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners think wasted energy disappears; it is transferred to the surroundings, mostly as thermal energy. Efficiency can never exceed 100% because of conservation of energy. Present efficiency as a percentage or decimal consistently.
